brief.headline: Memory supercycle extending into H2'26; HBM4 ramp, DRAM/NAND pricing power, hyperscaler capex surge all confirm multi-year upcycle
brief.summary: <cite index="1-5">Global semiconductor market projected to grow 25% YoY in 2026 to ~$975B, with memory up 30%</cite>. <cite index="10-7,16-15">DRAM contract prices rising 58-63% QoQ in Q2'26, NAND 70-75% QoQ</cite> following <cite index="12-1">Q1'26 DRAM surge of 90-95% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="21-9">Four hyperscalers spending ~$700B capex in 2026, nearly double 2025</cite>, with <cite index="30-2,30-6">TSMC's CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked through 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-1">SK Hynix held 57% HBM market share in Q4'25, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%</cite>, but <cite index="9-6,9-9">Samsung shipped HBM4E samples this week, >20% faster than HBM4, three months after HBM4 launch</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="36-3">SK Hynix market cap reached 93.2% of Samsung's on May 31, up from 46.5% a year ago</cite>, with <cite index="36-5">YTD gains of 258% for SK Hynix vs 164% for Samsung</cite>. SK Hynix retains HBM3E dominance (<cite index="1-11">62% shipment share Q2'25, 57% revenue Q3</cite>) and <cite index="1-17">UBS forecasts ~70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026</cite>. Samsung closing gap: <cite index="2-5">HBM4 passed Nvidia testing</cite>, <cite index="2-14">achieved 11.7Gbps speeds internally</cite>, and <cite index="38-8">customers stating 'Samsung is back' on HBM4</cite>. Long SK Hynix / short Samsung still consensus, but risk/reward compressing fast given <cite index="41-3">Goldman 2028 targets: Samsung 610T won op profit, SK Hynix 454T won</cite>—Samsung multiple remains discounted. Watch for Samsung HBM4 qual timing and Nvidia Rubin allocation split in Q3.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-3,13-4">Supply-demand gap widening as DRAM manufacturers reallocate advanced nodes to server DRAM and HBM for AI</cite>. <cite index="11-24,11-25">HBM crowding out commodity DRAM capacity at 3-to-1 conversion ratio</cite>. <cite index="16-7">Meaningful NAND capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028</cite>. Pricing has legs: <cite index="11-7">analysts project memory price rally extending past 2028</cite>. <cite index="5-2,5-12">Samsung and SK Hynix prioritizing HBM4 ramp keeps HBM3E supply tight</cite>, supporting <cite index="5-4">HBM3E price hikes despite HBM4 entry in 2026</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-9">HBM3E to account for ~66% of total HBM shipments in 2026, HBM4 gradually increasing</cite>. <cite index="3-7,3-8">Nvidia Rubin launch H2'26, each processor using eight HBM4 stacks</cite>. <cite index="3-11,3-13">Nvidia recently asked suppliers about 16-layer HBM delivery in Q4'26, with performance evaluation starting before Q3</cite>. <cite index="2-6,2-7">Samsung starting HBM4 mass production at Pyeongtaek in Feb'26; SK Hynix also ramping same timeframe</cite>. <cite index="2-16">HBM production capacities of both Samsung and SK Hynix already sold out for next year</cite>. <cite index="8-3">Samsung plans 250K wafers/month HBM capacity by end-2026, up 47% from 170K current</cite>. <cite index="5-5,5-8">H200 export approval to China boosting HBM3E demand; Google TPU and Amazon Trainium shipments in 2026 both using HBM3E</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung ships HBM4E samples, 20%+ faster than HBM4
news_pulse.implication: Samsung accelerating roadmap—HBM4E sampling three months after HBM4 launch signals aggressive push to close SK Hynix gap. 12-layer HBM4E uses 1c DRAM + 4nm base die. If Nvidia quals fast, Samsung could recapture share in H2'26 Rubin ramp.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix market cap hits 93% of Samsung, narrowest gap ever
news_pulse.implication: Relative valuation stretched. Hana Securities warned SK Hynix overtaking Samsung could signal bull market top, citing 2000 Cisco analog. YTD: SK Hynix +258%, Samsung +164%. Pair trade compression risk rising.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex hitting $700-725B in 2026, up ~67% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Demand visibility through 2027. Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet all raising guidance in April earnings. Two-thirds of capex going to short-lived assets (GPUs/CPUs), sustaining HBM/DRAM demand. Free cash flow compressing but ROIC still rising.

news_pulse.headline: Q2'26 DRAM prices up 58-63% QoQ, NAND 70-75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum intact after Q1's 90-95% DRAM surge. NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle. Enterprise SSD shortage persisting; client SSD buyers restocking preemptively. Supplier discipline holding—no panic capacity adds.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked through 2026
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains bottleneck. TSMC targeting 130K wafers/month by end-2026 (up from 35K late-2024). Nvidia securing >60% of 2025-26 capacity. Samsung/SK Hynix HBM output gated by CoWoS access, not die supply.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E pricing power persists despite HBM4 launch. H200 China export approval and hyperscaler ASIC ramps (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium) absorbing supply. 2026 HBM revenue mix forecast: 55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E starting Q3.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman raises Samsung + SK Hynix 2028 op profit view to >1,000T won combined
news_pulse.implication: Street extending supercycle duration. Goldman sees 'Higher for Longer' phase for DRAM/NAND/HBM, citing structural AI demand. 2028 targets: Samsung 610T won, SK Hynix 454T won—up 21-23% from prior forecast. Price targets: Samsung 450K won, SK Hynix 3.5M won.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI hits record 8,788 on retail ETF surge into Samsung/SK Hynix
news_pulse.implication: Retail frenzy warning flag. Single-stock leveraged ETFs drew 28T won in three days, with Samsung/SK Hynix leverage products dominating volume. ETF rebalancing driving institutional spot buying. Technical setup bullish but sentiment overheated—watch for vol spike.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="44-15,44-22">KODEX SK Hynix Single-Stock Leverage drew 10.9T won three-day volume, TIGER SK Hynix 1.3T won net retail inflow</cite>. <cite index="44-20">Retail sold 56% of leveraged ETF purchases within three days</cite>, signaling short-term momentum chasing. <cite index="42-22">Samsung single-stock leverage product surged ~20% on June 1</cite>. <cite index="45-1,45-2">Korea Exchange launching weekly options for Samsung, SK Hynix, Hyundai Motor, LG Energy on June 29</cite>. Implied vol likely elevated; consider selling upside calls in SK Hynix (258% YTD) vs buying Samsung calls (164% YTD) to fade relative momentum and capture theta. Watch for gamma squeeze risk around weekly expiries post-launch.
watch_for_next_3h: Jensen Huang Korea visit (expected ~June 5): meetings with Samsung, SK Hynix, LG, Naver, Hyundai. Any HBM4 allocation commentary or Rubin design-in announcements.
Samsung HBM4E customer feedback: timeline to Nvidia/Broadcom qual completion. HBM4 vs HBM4E positioning for H2'26 Rubin and 2027 ramp.
KOSPI 9,000 test: retail leveraged ETF flows and institutional rebalancing dynamics. Single-stock weekly options launch June 29 could amplify intraday volatility.
TrendForce June DRAM/NAND spot pricing update (due early June): confirm Q2 contract price trajectory and Q3 outlook. Watch DDR5 vs DDR4 spread and enterprise SSD allocation.
